News reporting from around September 8-10, 2026 indicates NPS now expects the damaged South Rim water supply system to be restored in weeks rather than months, but this does not change trail status. north-kaibab-coconino.note: The entirety of North Kaibab Trail, Phantom Ranch (including Bright Angel Campground, the Canteen, and cabins), and the Black Bridge and Silver Bridge river crossings remain closed with no estimated reopening, confirmed unchanged against the NPS Key Hiking Messages page, still last updated September 10, 2026 as of today's check (Source: National Park Service). The closure follows the severe flash flood that struck Bright Angel Canyon on August 29, destroying nearly all footbridges over Bright Angel Creek and damaging the Transcanyon pipeline that supplies South Rim water. News reporting from around September 8-10, 2026 indicates crews are building a temporary water intake at Bright Angel Creek and now expect water service restoration to take weeks rather than months, since the flood spared most of the nearly complete replacement pipeline, but this does not change trail or Phantom Ranch closure status. Phantom Ranch reservations remain cancelled and Colorado River traffic through the area remains halted. The National Park Service continues to warn that additional thunderstorms could bring further flash flooding, debris flows, and rockfall with little to no warning. No NWS Excessive Heat Warning is active for Grand Canyon country today; no active NWS alerts were found for the area today (Source: National Weather Service). Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park.
